warnings.message: Topic has no hard prerequisites and is not marked foundational.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Match and sort shapes
node.description: Match, sort and describe shapes and objects using everyday and mathematical attributes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Name common two-dimensional shapes
node.description: Recognise and name circles, triangles, rectangles, squares and other common two-dimensional shapes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Name common three-dimensional objects
node.description: Recognise and name cubes, spheres, cones, cylinders, prisms and pyramids in everyday contexts.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Flat shapes versus solid objects
node.description: Distinguish flat two-dimensional shapes from solid three-dimensional objects.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Shape orientation invariance
node.description: Recognise that a shape remains the same type when shown in a different orientation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sides and vertices
node.description: Identify and count sides and vertices of two-dimensional shapes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polygons and non-polygons
node.description: Distinguish polygons from non-polygons using straight sides and closed shape criteria.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle types
node.description: Classify triangles by sides and angles using appropriate geometric language.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Quadrilateral types
node.description: Classify quadrilaterals such as squares, rectangles, rhombuses, parallelograms, trapezia and kites by their properties.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel and perpendicular sides
node.description: Identify parallel and perpendicular side relationships in two-dimensional shapes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Symmetry properties of shapes
node.description: Describe line and rotational symmetry properties of common two-dimensional shapes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Circle parts
node.description: Identify centre, radius, diameter and circumference as parts of a circle.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Faces edges and vertices
node.description: Identify and count faces, edges and vertices of three-dimensional objects.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Prisms and pyramids
node.description: Classify prisms and pyramids by bases, faces, edges and vertices.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Curved surfaces
node.description: Describe objects with curved surfaces such as spheres, cylinders and cones.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nets of solids
node.description: Connect three-dimensional objects with two-dimensional nets that fold to make them.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Views of solids
node.description: Interpret front, side and top views of simple three-dimensional objects.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Build solids from unit cubes
node.description: Build and interpret simple solids made from unit cubes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Euler relationship introduction
node.description: Explore the relationship between faces, edges and vertices for simple polyhedra.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Hierarchical shape classification
node.description: Classify shapes using inclusive property relationships, such as squares as rectangles and rhombuses.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Plan views and models
node.description: Relate simple models of objects to plan views and sketches.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Attributes define shape categories
node.description: Shapes and objects can be classified by defining attributes rather than colour, size or orientation.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Two-dimensional shapes are flat
node.description: Two-dimensional shapes are flat figures with length and width but no thickness.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Three-dimensional objects are solid
node.description: Three-dimensional objects have length, width and height or depth.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Sides and vertices are shape features
node.description: Sides and vertices help describe and classify two-dimensional shapes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel sides are a property
node.description: Parallel side relationships help classify quadrilaterals and other polygons.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Faces edges and vertices describe objects
node.description: Faces, edges and vertices are structural features of many three-dimensional objects.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nets show connected faces
node.description: A net shows the faces of a solid arranged so they can fold to form the object.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Shape classes can overlap
node.description: A shape can belong to more than one class when it satisfies multiple sets of properties.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Circle has centre radius and diameter
node.description: A circle can be described by its centre, radius and diameter.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Views represent three-dimensional objects
node.description: Front, side and top views can represent different aspects of a three-dimensional object.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Orientation changes shape type
node.description: Learner thinks a differently oriented shape is a different kind of shape.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Flat solid confusion
node.description: Learner confuses flat shapes with solid objects, such as calling a cube a square.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Square is not a rectangle
node.description: Learner treats shape categories as exclusive and does not recognise squares as special rectangles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Count faces edges vertices inconsistently
node.description: Learner double-counts or omits faces, edges or vertices when describing objects.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Net faces not connected correctly
node.description: Learner draws or selects separated or incorrectly connected faces that cannot fold into the object.

edge.rationale: Matching and sorting are core early shape identification practices.
Naming common 2D shapes is central to shape identification.
Naming common 3D objects is central to object identification.
Distinguishing flat shapes and solid objects supports accurate identification.
Recognising shapes across orientations improves robust identification.
Sides and vertices are core 2D shape properties.
Polygon criteria support classification of 2D shapes.
Triangle classification is a key 2D shape property topic.
Quadrilateral classification is central to 2D shape properties.
Parallel and perpendicular relationships support property-based classification.
Symmetry is an important property of many 2D shapes.
Circle parts support later circle measurement and geometry.
Hierarchical classification deepens property-based shape reasoning.
Faces, edges and vertices are core properties of 3D objects.
Prisms and pyramids are central classes of 3D objects.
Curved surfaces distinguish spheres, cylinders and cones from polyhedra.
Nets connect 3D object structure to 2D faces.
Views of solids support spatial reasoning about 3D objects.
Building solids from unit cubes supports concrete 3D structure reasoning.
Euler relationships are an optional extension of face-edge-vertex reasoning in simple polyhedra.
Plan views and models connect 3D objects to 2D representations.
Sorting shapes uses attribute focus, though early spatial sorting also develops independently.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sorts by colour or size when shape property is the target.

edge.rationale: Naming common 2D shapes builds from matching and sorting examples by shape attributes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner recognises matches but cannot name common shapes consistently.

edge.rationale: Naming common 3D objects builds from sorting and recognising object forms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner recognises similar objects but cannot name common solids consistently.

edge.rationale: Distinguishing flat and solid forms requires recognising examples of flat shapes first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calls solids by names of their faces or treats pictures as objects.

edge.rationale: Recognising a shape across orientations builds on recognising the shape in familiar orientations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner says a tilted square is not a square or a rotated triangle is a different shape.

edge.rationale: Identifying sides and vertices builds on recognising common 2D shapes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot identify or count sides and corners consistently.

edge.rationale: Polygon criteria require recognising straight sides, vertices and closed boundaries.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats open shapes or curved shapes as polygons.

edge.rationale: Triangle classification requires recognising triangles as three-sided polygons.
edge.failure_signal: Learner classifies by appearance only rather than side or angle properties.

edge.rationale: Quadrilateral classification requires recognising four-sided polygons and their properties.
edge.failure_signal: Learner does not distinguish rectangles, squares and other four-sided shapes by properties.

edge.rationale: Parallel and perpendicular side properties are commonly introduced through quadrilateral classification.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies sides but not their direction relationships.

edge.rationale: Shape symmetry properties require recognising and describing 2D shape structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies a shape but cannot test or describe its symmetry.

edge.rationale: Circle-part vocabulary builds on recognising circles as 2D shapes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot locate the centre, radius or diameter in a circle diagram.

edge.rationale: Faces, edges and vertices are properties of recognised 3D objects.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses faces with edges or vertices or cannot locate them on a solid.

edge.rationale: Prism and pyramid classification uses base, face, edge and vertex structure.
edge.failure_signal: Learner classifies solids by overall appearance only rather than structural features.

edge.rationale: Recognising curved surfaces builds on recognising common solids such as spheres, cylinders and cones.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats curved surfaces as flat faces or cannot distinguish spheres from cylinders.

edge.rationale: Nets of solids require understanding the object's faces and how they connect.
edge.failure_signal: Learner draws faces but cannot arrange them so they fold into the object.

edge.rationale: Interpreting views requires understanding 3D objects and their visible faces.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses a face view with the full object.

edge.rationale: Building solids from unit cubes uses the same unit-cube structure as volume models.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot infer hidden cubes or keep layers aligned.

edge.rationale: Euler relationship exploration depends on consistently counting faces, edges and vertices.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot test relationships because counts are inconsistent.

edge.rationale: Hierarchical classification builds on knowing quadrilateral properties and recognising overlapping categories.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats square, rectangle and rhombus categories as mutually exclusive without considering definitions.

edge.rationale: Plan views and models build from interpreting front, side and top views of objects.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect a simple model with its plan view or sketch.
